title: Classic Marinara Sauce
trouble: Simmer for an extra 10 minutes or add a tiny pinch more salt to balance it.
Discard the oil and garlic, wipe the pan clean, and start over with lower heat.
goes: Pasta, polenta, or as a base for poached eggs

steps.t: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
steps.w: To create a base for sautéing without burning the garlic.
steps.c: Oil shimmers and flows easily; 2 mins
steps.m: Overheating until it smokes, which makes the sauce bitter.
steps.img: Close-up of golden olive oil shimmering in a stainless steel pan over a burner.

steps.t: Add the sliced garlic and sauté until fragrant.
steps.w: To release aromatic oils from the garlic.
steps.c: Garlic becomes translucent and smells nutty, not brown; 2 mins
steps.m: Letting the garlic turn dark brown or black, which ruins the flavor.
steps.img: Close-up of thinly sliced garlic cloves sizzling in olive oil.

steps.t: Pour in the crushed tomatoes and stir in the salt.
steps.w: To combine the base with the main body of the sauce.
steps.c: A thick, bubbling red mixture; 1 min
steps.m: Splashing hot tomato sauce on skin by pouring too quickly.
steps.img: Close-up of crushed canned tomatoes being poured into a pan with garlic.

steps.t: Stir in the dried oregano and simmer on low heat.
steps.w: To allow flavors to meld and the acidity of the tomato to mellow.
steps.c: Sauce thickens slightly and smells herbal; 15 mins
steps.m: Boiling too vigorously, which causes the sauce to splatter and separate.
steps.img: Close-up of a bubbling red tomato sauce simmering gently in a pan.

steps.t: Remove from heat and stir in the torn fresh basil.
steps.w: Fresh herbs lose flavor if cooked too long; adding at the end preserves brightness.
steps.c: Bright green leaves folded into deep red sauce; 1 min
steps.m: Adding basil while the pan is still on high heat, wilting it instantly.
steps.img: Close-up of fresh green basil leaves being stirred into a thick red marinara sauce.

title: Mediterranean Lemon-Garlic Halloumi and Green Bean Sauté
trouble: Rinse the halloumi slices under cold water for 30 seconds before frying to remove excess surface brine.
Add a tablespoon of water and cover with a lid for 2 minutes to steam them slightly before adding garlic.
goes: A side of fresh tomato slices or a simple lemon-parsley garnish.

steps.t: Heat a splash of olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken until golden brown, about 6-8 minutes. Remove from pan and set aside.
steps.w: To cook the protein separately as per dietary requirements.
steps.c: Golden crust on meat; smells savory; 7 mins
steps.m: Overcrowding the pan which causes steaming instead of searing.
steps.img: Close-up of cubed chicken breast searing in a stainless steel skillet, golden brown edges, glistening oil, photo-realistic.

steps.t: In the same pan (or a clean one), add olive oil and sauté the green beans. For Alex's portion, add cauliflower; for Sam's, add baby potatoes.
steps.w: To cook the base vegetables and handle the carb/veg swap.
steps.c: Beans turn bright green; potatoes slightly softened; 8 mins
steps.m: Adding garlic too early, which will cause it to burn before veg are tender.
steps.img: Close-up of bright green beans and cauliflower florets sautéing in olive oil in a pan, photo-realistic.

steps.t: Stir in the minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
steps.w: Garlic burns quickly; adding it late preserves flavor.
steps.m: Leaving the pan unattended, leading to burnt bitter garlic.
steps.img: Close-up of minced garlic and dried oregano being stirred into green vegetables in a skillet, photo-realistic.

steps.t: Either: Push the vegetables to the side. Add another splash of oil if needed and fry the halloumi slices until golden on both sides.
steps.w: Halloumi is best when charred and squeaky.
steps.c: Golden brown crust on cheese; 4 mins
steps.m: Flipping too early before a crust forms, causing the cheese to stick.
steps.img: Close-up of halloumi slices frying in a pan next to green beans, golden brown sear marks, photo-realistic.

steps.t: Drizzle lemon juice over everything and stir gently to combine. Return the cooked chicken to Alex's side of the pan.
steps.w: Acid from lemon balances the saltiness of halloumi and richness of oil.
steps.c: Sizzling sound as lemon hits hot pan; glossy finish; 2 mins
steps.m: Adding lemon too early, which can prevent browning in some steps.
steps.img: Close-up of fresh lemon juice being poured over a mixture of halloumi and green beans, steam rising, photo-realistic.

steps.t: Make the sauce: lift everything onto the plates. Pour 3 tbsp water into the hot pan, scrape the brown chicken and halloumi bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon and let it bubble 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in 1 tbsp olive oil, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of oregano with a fork until cloudy, then spoon the sauce over.
steps.w: The brown bits hold the flavour, and lemon and oil turn them into a light Greek sauce.
steps.c: It is cloudy and slightly thick, not just oil sitting on water.
steps.m: Leaving the brown bits stuck to the pan, where all the taste is.

title: Slow-Cooker Mediterranean Vegetable Stew with Lemon and Oregano
trouble: Simmer on High for 30 minutes without the lid to reduce liquid.
Add a pinch more salt or a small knob of butter during reheating.
goes: Crusty whole-grain bread or a side of fresh greens.

steps.t: Sauté the diced onion and carrot in olive oil in a pan until softened to build a flavor base.
steps.c: Onions look translucent and smell sweet; 6 minutes.
steps.m: Burning the onions by using heat that is too high.
steps.img: Close-up of diced onions and carrots softening in golden olive oil in a stainless steel pan.

steps.t: Transfer sautéed vegetables to the slow cooker; add the green beans, red bell pepper, minced garlic, canned tomatoes, vegetable stock, oregano, salt and pepper.
steps.w: Combining all base ingredients for slow infusion.
steps.c: A thick, colorful mixture of vegetables and red sauce; 5 minutes.
steps.m: Forgetting to add the stock, which may cause burning.
steps.img: Close-up of a ceramic slow cooker pot filled with chopped Mediterranean vegetables, diced tomatoes, and herbs.

steps.t: Cover and cook on Low for 8 hours (or High for 4 hours). Make the sauce at the end: press a few pieces of tomato and carrot against the side with a spoon and stir for 2 minutes until the liquid thickens, then stir in the lemon juice.
steps.w: Slow cooking breaks down fibers while preserving nutrients.
steps.c: Vegetables are tender but not mushy; smells lemony and herby; 8 hours.
steps.m: Adding lemon juice at the start, which can make it taste bitter.
steps.img: Close-up of a bubbling, rich vegetable stew in a slow cooker with steam rising.

steps.t: While the stew finishes, sear cubed chicken in a pan until golden brown and boil the quinoa according to the package instructions.
steps.w: Cooking proteins and grains separately to maintain texture and dietary needs.
steps.c: Chicken is browned on all sides; quinoa is fluffy; 15 minutes.
steps.m: Overcooking the chicken, making it dry.
steps.img: Split screen: golden brown chicken cubes in a pan and a pot of fluffy white quinoa.

steps.t: For the low-carb swap, steam or sauté cauliflower florets until tender-crisp.
steps.w: Replacing grains with a vegetable to meet net carb limits.
steps.c: Cauliflower is pale white and slightly softened; 7 minutes.
steps.img: Close-up of steamed, tender cauliflower florets in a colander.

steps.t: Divide the vegetable stew into 6 containers. Add quinoa to Sam's containers and cauliflower + seared chicken to Alex's.
steps.w: Meal prep organization for the week.
steps.c: Six equal portions distributed in airtight containers; 10 minutes.
steps.m: Mixing all proteins into one pot, ruining the vegetarian base.
steps.img: Top-down view of six meal prep containers filled with vegetable stew, some with quinoa and others with chicken and cauliflower.

title: Beef Bourguignon
ing: peeled and sliced into thick rounds

steps.t: Heat olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and fry bacon lardons until crisp.
steps.img: Close up of diced bacon sizzling in a cast iron pot with golden oil.

steps.t: Remove bacon and sear beef chuck in the fat until browned on all sides.
steps.img: Close up of brown seared beef cubes in a pot.

steps.t: Add carrots and onion to the pot and sauté until softened.
steps.img: Close up of sliced carrots and diced onions softening in a pot with beef.

steps.t: Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste, cooking for one minute.
steps.img: Close up of a wooden spoon stirring red tomato paste into vegetables.

steps.t: Sprinkle flour over the meat and vegetables, stirring well to coat.
steps.img: Close up of white flour being dusted over beef and carrots.

steps.t: Pour in beef stock and red wine vinegar, scraping the bottom of the pot.
steps.img: Close up of brown stock being poured into a pot, deglazing the bottom.

steps.t: Add salt, black pepper, and the cooked bacon back into the pot.
steps.img: Close up of salt and pepper being sprinkled over a stew.

steps.t: Cover with a lid and place in a fan oven at 160°C for 2.5 hours.
steps.img: Close up of a heavy pot with a lid being slid into an oven.

steps.t: Remove from oven and stir in butter to thicken and glaze the sauce.
steps.img: Close up of a knob of butter melting into a rich brown beef stew.

steps.t: In a bowl, mix the olive oil, lemon juice, dried oregano, salt, black pepper, and garlic.
steps.img: Close-up of a glass bowl with olive oil, lemon juice, and herbs being whisked by a spoon.

steps.t: Add the chicken breast to the marinade and stir until every piece is coated.
steps.img: Hands stirring cubed raw chicken in a yellow-green herb marinade.

steps.t: Cover the bowl and let the chicken marinate in the fridge.
steps.img: A covered glass bowl of marinated chicken sitting on a refrigerator shelf.

steps.t: Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto wooden skewers.
steps.img: Close-up of hands sliding cubed chicken onto wooden skewers.

steps.t: Heat a grill pan or frying pan over medium-high heat until very hot.
steps.img: A cast iron grill pan heating up on a stove burner.

steps.t: Place the skewers in the pan and sear without moving them for 3 minutes.
steps.img: Chicken skewers searing in a hot pan with visible grill marks forming.

steps.t: Turn the skewers and cook for another 4-5 minutes until golden brown.
steps.img: Tongs flipping chicken skewers in a pan, juices bubbling.

steps.t: Remove the skewers from the heat and let them rest on a plate.
steps.img: Finished golden-brown chicken skewers resting on a white ceramic plate.

steps.t: Mix olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
steps.img: Close-up of hands mixing oil and dried herbs in a glass bowl.

steps.t: Coat the chicken breast in the herb mixture.
steps.img: Hands rubbing a green herb oil marinade into raw chicken breasts.

steps.t: Heat a pan over medium-high heat and sear the chicken for 6-8 minutes per side until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
steps.img: Close-up of golden brown grilled chicken breasts searing in a pan.

steps.t: Combine strained Greek yogurt and minced garlic in a bowl.
steps.img: Mixing thick white yogurt with tiny bits of minced garlic.

steps.t: Stir in the grated zucchini and lemon juice.
steps.img: Adding green shredded zucchini into a bowl of white yogurt.

steps.t: Season the sauce with a pinch of salt and pepper.
steps.img: Sprinkling salt over a bowl of creamy tzatziki.

steps.t: Let the chicken rest on a plate for 5 minutes before slicing.
steps.img: Grilled chicken breasts resting on a white ceramic plate.

steps.t: Serve the sliced chicken alongside a generous scoop of the sauce.
steps.img: Plated grilled chicken slices next to a bowl of creamy tzatziki.
